def anti_shuffle(s):
    return ' '.join([''.join(sorted(list(i))) for i in s.split(' ')])

# Unit test for function anti_shuffle
def test_anti_shuffle():
    # Single word already sorted
    assert anti_shuffle("Hi") == "Hi"
    
    # Single word needing sorting
    assert anti_shuffle("hello") == "ehllo"
    
    # Multiple words
    assert anti_shuffle("Hello World!!!") == "Hello !!!Wdlor"
    
    # Empty string
    assert anti_shuffle("") == ""
    
    # Case sensitivity: uppercase sorts before lowercase (ASCII)
    assert anti_shuffle("baCa") == "Caba"
    
    # Numbers and symbols
    assert anti_shuffle("321!@#") == "!@#123"
    
    # Multiple consecutive spaces are preserved
    assert anti_shuffle("a b  c") == "a b  c"
    
    # Two unsorted words
    assert anti_shuffle("dcba hgfe") == "abcd efgh"
    
    # Single character
    assert anti_shuffle("z") == "z"
    
    # Sentence example
    assert anti_shuffle("This is a test") == "This is a estt"
    
    print("All tests passed!")

test_anti_shuffle()
